newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Czestochowa seeks bourse listing. [CORRECTED 13:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Czestochowa seeks bourse listing. [CORRECTED 13:39 GMT]

text.p: Poland's Bank Czestochowa SA plans a public offering and a Warsaw bourse listing this year or next, depending on whether it first issues shares to an investor group, a bank management board member said on Thursday.
(Corrects source of statement from "the bank's president" to "a bank management board member".)

"This year we want to raise 10 million zlotys in either a public offering or a placement, but if our shareholders choose the latter...then next year there would be a several-million-zloty public offering," Dariusz Salajewski told Reuters.
He said shareholders would decide in 1997's first half.

Salajewski said the bank, which would likely enter the parallel market, needed the money to expand operations at its southern-Polish base around the town of Czestochowa, buy equipment and possibly launch foreign-exchange transactions.

He said the bank's largest shareholders were the Huta Katowice steel mill, the Czestochowa municipality and the state treasury, with 43.1 percent, 22.2 percent and 15.5 percent of shareholder votes respectively.

Salajewski said that after two smaller closed issues early this year, in which Bank Komunalny would gain below five percent of the bank, Czestochowa's own funds would rise to around eight million zlotys from the current 6.6 million.
He said Czestochowa planned to up last year's 1.3-million-zloty net profit to 1.7 million zlotys this year, not taking into consideration the planned capital raises.
